subject: ela
cluster: Range of reading and level of text complexity
intro: Third graders read stories, dramas, and poems and understand them, using all their reading skills together: finding key details, the theme, characters, and the meaning of words. A good reader asks questions and checks the text for answers.

items.prompt:
Read.

The little ant worked all summer gathering food, while the grasshopper played. When winter came, the ant had plenty, but the grasshopper was hungry.

What lesson does this story teach?

steps: I think about what the story shows.
The ant who worked was ready; the one who played was not.
So the lesson is that hard work and planning pay off.
solution.answer: Hard work and planning pay off.

items.prompt:
Read (same story).

Who was NOT ready for winter, and why?

steps: The grasshopper played instead of gathering food.
So the grasshopper was not ready because it did not work.
solution.answer: The grasshopper, because it played instead of gathering food.

items.prompt:
Read.

Maya was scared to try the diving board, but she took a deep breath and jumped. When she came up smiling, she felt proud.

How does Maya change in the story?

steps: After she jumps, she feels proud.
So she changes from scared to proud/brave.
solution.answer: She goes from scared to proud and brave.

items.prompt:
Read.

Tom shared his umbrella with a wet puppy and smiled.

What kind of character is Tom?

steps: He shares and smiles, so he is kind.

items.prompt:
Read.

The seed grew slowly, but with water and sun it became a strong tree.

What helped the seed grow?
